title: GH#37005: fail over primary sessions after model entitlement rejection
body:
## Summary

Resolves #37005

Add root interactive/ACP entitlement recovery at the existing OpenCode chat/error hooks. Reuse the auth-scoped model TTL and connected same-tier routing selector; never change routing tiers, credentials or local-only egress controls.

Recovery waits for the failed assistant to complete and the run to become idle, rather than joining the original failing run. Concurrent client retries cannot request the rejected model during recovery. Generated turns, child/headless sessions, and internal/out-of-table requests cannot trigger an unsafe replay.

Exhaustion emits one native error notification naming the rejected model and the re-authentication/routing next steps. Subsequent ACP/client attempts fail in `chat.message` before a provider request; Buzz's own retry policy is unchanged and remains upstream/out of scope.

## Files and reference

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/primary-entitlement-failover.mjs`: primary recovery, referencing `subagent-entitlement-failover.mjs`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort.mjs`: compose primary and child handlers at the already-wired hooks.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/specialist-advisor.mjs`: daily-driver route selection and connected candidate walk, separated from lifecycle handling to repair the initial CI complexity findings.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs`: six focused primary regression cases alongside the existing child coverage.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Level: runtime-verified through the plugin handlers and provider-rejection boundary, not a live Buzz desktop session.

- Node v24.22.1; OpenCode v1.19.5.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-specialist-advisor.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-error-diagnostics.mjs`: 83 passed, zero failures.

After that repair, a full rerun reported 1312 passed, one skipped, and one unrelated MCP output-confinement test failure (`ENOENT` for its generated Playwright fixture). - Native Buzz end-to-end was not exercised. Plugin changes apply to newly started OpenCode/ACP processes after deployment, not this running worker.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Definite primary rejection resumes the same session on a connected same-tier candidate | Satisfied | Primary rejection test exercises the real fetch-boundary marker and hook-driven prompt; SDK `id` normalization and failed-run teardown are covered |
| Rejected model is not requested again within auth TTL; no lower tier or out-of-table fallback | Satisfied | Cached/disconnected candidate, exhaustion/deduplication and auth-change tests; shared selector retains local-only policy |
| Exhaustion names rejected model and recovery action without another provider request | Satisfied | Single native notification and fail-fast client hook are asserted; no change to upstream Buzz retries |
| Existing child behavior and touched tests pass | Satisfied | 83 scoped cases pass; full-suite transient MCP fixture failure and passing isolated rerun are documented above |

title: GH#36626: reconstructible retirement must not retain ignored files
body:
## Summary

Ref #36626 (closed). The remote-reconstructible retirement class added in #36631 also rejected worktrees containing **ignored** files (`git status --ignored`). The issue asked only for "Clean, including untracked files"; ignored files were added by the worker as a conservative choice ("Ignored files are retained conservatively").

Effect in production: practically every awardsapp/aidevops worktree contains ignored artefacts (`node_modules`, `.turbo`, `__pycache__`, `.husky/_`, `.agents/loop-state`), so every candidate was retained as `nonempty-worktree-state`. On two Linux runners the registry has **zero** `reconstructible-*` events — the class never retired anything, not even the first per-host probe.

## Change

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_inventory.py`: drop `--ignored` from the cleanliness check. Tracked, untracked and submodule state still retain the source.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`: split the test — untracked files still retain; ignored files (via `info/exclude`) no longer retain and the worktree retires.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`: document that ignored files do not retain.

This matches the existing policy in `CLEANUP.md` ("Ignored files are deliberately discarded with the worktree, never archived"). Non-forced `git worktree remove` already discards ignored files and refuses on untracked/modified tracked files, so the removal path is unchanged. All other guards (lock, remote containment, open PR, preservation names, `/proc` census, host probe) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `umask 022; python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_reconstructible tests.test_legacy_cleanup` (in `.agents/worker-lifecycle`): 61 tests, OK.
- Under the default Ubuntu `umask 002`, 22 tests error with `unsafe-repository-config` both on `main` and on this branch — pre-existing, caused by `cleanup.py` rejecting group-writable configs even for user-private groups. Tracked separately (consolidating permission checks into `filesystem.py`).
- Production evidence: registry event census on two runners (0 `reconstructible-*` events); read-only automatic preview on one runner.

title: refactor(lifecycle): single permission-check library; accept user-private-group configs
body:
## Summary

Lifecycle mode-bit checks were hand-written in several modules with different rules. `cleanup.py` rejected `repos.json` on `st_mode & 0o022`, so on Ubuntu/Debian (user-private groups, `umask 002`) a `0664` config owned by the user and their private group stopped cleanup with `unsafe-repository-config`, while `filesystem.py` already accepted exactly that case for directories. The same rule was also copied inline in `enrollment.py`.

This PR moves every permission decision in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/` into public functions in `filesystem.py`:

| Function | Rule |
|---|---|
| `is_private_mode(info)` | no group/other bits |
| `group_write_is_private(target, info)` | owned + `user_private_group(gid)` + no POSIX access ACL |
| `shared_writable(target, info)` | other-write, or group-write that is not private |
| `read_owned_file(path, *, reason, max_size, private, single_link=True)` | `O_NOFOLLOW` read of a bounded regular file owned by the user; raises `FilesystemValidationError(reason)` with a `violation` (`wrong-type`, `wrong-owner`, `multiple-links`, `too-large`, `not-private`, `shared-writable`) |

Call sites switched:
- `cleanup._repository_entries` → `read_owned_file(private=False)`. **Behaviour change:** user-private-group write is accepted; shared groups, other-write and ACLs are still refused.
- `enrollment._git_directory` → `shared_writable` (identical rule, local wrappers removed).
- `enrollment._read_marker` → `read_owned_file(private=True, single_link=False)` (identical rule).
- `archive_path.validate_archive_path`, `filesystem.validate_private_path`, `filesystem._group_write_is_private` → shared predicates (identical rules).

Reason codes are unchanged. Errors are now `FilesystemValidationError` (a `ValueError` subclass), so existing handlers in `cleanup_failure.py`/`cli_errors.py` also report the path and the violation.

Out of scope: owner-only checks on worktree paths (`legacy_inventory.py:122`, `legacy_options.py:66`), `/proc` UID checks (`linux.py`), the retirement lock identity check, and shell-side permission checks in `.agents/scripts/`.

## Verification

- `umask 002; python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle`: **343 tests, OK** (before: 22+ `unsafe-repository-config` errors plus `test_group_write_requires_private_group_or_sealed_ancestor` failing under the same umask).
- New `test_read_owned_file_accepts_only_private_group_write`: private group accepted; shared group, ACL present, other-write, non-private when `private=True`, hard links and oversize refused.
- `test_enrollment` now patches `worker_lifecycle.filesystem.user_private_group` (the single definition).
- `ruff check --isolated --select E4,E7,E9,F,B --target-version py310` on changed files: passes (the pinned 0.11.13 is unavailable locally; CI runs it).

## Summary

Root cause: the classic settings read in _required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached only fell back to the readable branch-metadata endpoint (GH#34965) when the captured error text matched 404 markers. On the supervisor runner the read returns exit 1 without those markers, so every merge cycle failed closed on a ruleset-only private repo and CI-drift kept re-running CI. Reproduction through the real stack (shared-constants + shared-gh-wrappers + _gh_with_timeout, with the repo gh PATH shim and native gh 2.103.3) on this runner preserves 'gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)' on both consecutive calls; 404 is never recorded as a cooldown (cooldown only records 403/429/remaining=0/secondary text), so the exact production layer that drops the marker could not be identified from this runner. The fix therefore removes the dependency on error text instead of guessing a layer: (1) exit 75 (local admission/cooldown) and exit 124 (timeout) are logged as deferrals ('branch protection read deferred locally' / 'timed out') and spend no further read; (2) every other settings failure falls back to branch metadata, which is independent, authoritative evidence (protected=false -> no classic contexts; protected with a valid required_status_checks shape -> those contexts; anything else fails closed); (3) unclassified recoveries log 'branch metadata resolved classic requirements (GH#37026)' with a bounded exit/HTTP-status hint and no body, and unresolved ones still log 'branch protection API failed ... caller will fail closed'. shared-gh-wrappers.sh needed no change (the transport preserved the 404 in every reproduction). Step 4 (CI-drift rebase at most once per head) is out of this scope and is split to a follow-up issue.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-phantom-pending-checks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh: 114/114 pass, including new cases that source the real shared-constants.sh + shared-gh-wrappers.sh so _pmrc_gh_read runs through _gh_with_timeout (cooldown preflight, capture, replay, cooldown recording) and call _required_contexts_for_default_branch twice: native 404 shape (body on stdout, '(HTTP 404)' on stderr) and an unclassified exit-1 failure both resolve via branch metadata (pass/unprotected) or fail closed (unknown) on both calls; a local deferral (exit 75) fails closed as a deferral with no extra read. Against the origin/main version of pulse-merge-required-checks.sh the new unclassified/deferral cases fail (5 failures), proving the regression coverage. Scoped suites also pass: ruleset-fallback, gh-check-status-cache, preflight-snapshot, admin-safety-check, full-loop-merge-cases, update-branch, phantom-pending-checks (generic-error case now also fails the branch-metadata read to keep testing fail-closed), ci-repair-routing, primary-first-diagnostics, descriptor-safe-log. shellcheck -x: zero findings on the three changed files. Runtime: with the real PATH shim and native gh on this runner, _required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached against a ruleset-only private managed repo returned rc=0 with the four ruleset contexts on two consecutive calls and logged 'active rulesets add required contexts'.

Resolves #37026
